{
  "rules": [
    "If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent history, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.",
    "If sentiment is negative (≤0.0), model often underestimates drops; increase downward bias or add early correction factor.",
    "Model consistently overpredicts early in the 30-day horizon, especially after spikes; apply lagged correction by subtracting 1–2% from forecast for days 1–5.",
    "After a sharp price spike, model overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 5–10% in subsequent days post-spike.",
    "Model exhibits mean reversion bias — overestimates after low points, underestimates after high points; adjust forecast by aligning with 14-day moving average of history.",
    "Sentiment history with multiple 0.2 values suggests market is ‘overconfident’; reduce forecast growth rate by 0.5–1.0% per 0.2 sentiment point.",
    "If true outcome shows strong downward trend after forecast peak, model fails to anticipate; add early warning signal for 3–5 day downward drift."
  ]
}
